## RADD-znxdxgyh: extract_embeddings() chops 1e6 vctrs slices to deliver a handful

**Status:** done | **Parent:** pbwpleuzfntiksjhkjicnjrgyxkthhqd

### Description

Found by O1's classify benchmark (RADD-jyeuyxqs, docs/architecture.md 11.1.7).

`addr_classify()` on 1e6 IPv6 addresses is 13.9 s. The prefix lookups 11.1.6 tuned are 0.4 s of that. `extract_embeddings()` is 11.7 s, and profiled by line 11.58 s of 11.58 s is inside vctrs -- vec_proxy 62%, vec_chop 24% -- on a corpus where 19 rows of 1e6 had an embedding.

R/embedding.R:306-312 scatters its result back to one element per address as:

    vec_chop(rows, indices = split(seq_along(at), factor(at, levels = seq_len(n))))

Timed alone with 4 embedded rows of 1e6: factor() 0.131 s, split() 0.017 s, vec_chop() 11.685 s. It asks vctrs for a million slices of a nested record to deliver four, paying a vec_proxy() round-trip each.

THE COMPLEXITY IS THE FINDING. The shape is flat in the number of embeddings and linear in n: 11.1 s for 19 embedded rows, 12.2 s for 240,172. The two wall clocks are nearly equal, which is what hid it.

Candidate: chop only the groups that have rows, scatter into the prebuilt list of empties.

    groups <- split(seq_along(at), at)
    slots <- rep(list(empty), n)
    slots[as.integer(names(groups))] <- vec_chop(rows, indices = unname(groups))
    new_list_of(slots, ptype = empty)

Measured, identical() TRUE on both:
  19 rows of 1e6      11.137 s -> 0.005 s   2227x
  240,172 of 1e6      12.184 s -> 1.959 s      6.2x

Now linear in the embeddings rather than in n. Moves classify IPv6 from ~76x of the ipaddress predicate bundle to roughly the IPv4 row's 4x.

Not a blind win to take on faith: the list-of column is API surface (8.1) and must stay vctrs size-stable, empty rows must keep their empty rather than becoming zero-row-of-wrong-ptype, and Teredo is the two-rows-per-element case whose in-element order (server then client, RFC 4380 4) is asserted. Run the embedding and classify suites plus the size-stability invariants (11.4), not just the timing.

### Comments

#### 2026-07-29 — 142225707+bart-turczynski@users.noreply.github.com

Fixed in 116639e. addr_classify() on 1e6 IPv6 addresses: 13.878 s -> 0.882 s, 15.7x. Answers unchanged.

Measured after, via bench/classify.R:

                        before    after   / bundle before -> after
  IPv4 random           0.604 s   0.640 s   4.3x -> 4.5x  (untouched)
  IPv4 inside special   0.614 s   0.613 s   3.8x -> 3.8x  (untouched)
  IPv6 random          13.878 s   0.882 s  85.7x -> 5.5x
  IPv6 inside special  13.574 s   3.827 s  75.8x -> 21.5x

extract_embeddings() itself: 11.726 s -> 0.028 s (random), 16.677 s -> 2.215 s (inside blocks). The negative remainder is gone (-3.664 s -> 1.018 s), which confirms the earlier anomaly was the allocation destabilizing best-of-five rather than a subtraction error.

IPv4 is untouched by construction: with no transition formats it returns before the scatter.

Two departures from the candidate in the description, both deliberate:
- positions are sort(unique(at)), not names(split()), so integer positions are not round-tripped through the character names of a factor level;
- the scatter does not depend on 'at' being ascending even though order_in_element makes it so. An invariant deciding which address gets which embedding should not be held implicitly by a neighbouring sort.

Verified answer-identical rather than assumed. identical() TRUE against the pre-change code (via git stash, not a reimplementation) on: 1e6 random IPv6 rows; the 240,172-embedding inside-blocks corpus; and a hand-built corner corpus covering teredo's two rows per element with their asserted server-then-client order (RFC 4380 4), the deprecated 192.88.99.0/24 relay image with its NA policy, nat64_wk, ipv4_mapped, 4in6, empty rows interleaved between full ones, and embeddings on both the first and last element. Also checked size-stability, ptype preservation, and that empty rows stay the empty record.

Full test suite green (embedding, classify, transition, invariants, slow, property). Verify gate: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 pre-existing NOTE.

What remains on IPv6 is real work: 2.2 s on a corpus that puts an embedding on 20% of rows, each taking a recursive addr_classify() on the extracted IPv4 -- and that corpus samples the special-purpose registry uniformly, where real traffic touches the transition formats approximately never.
